title: A Signal for the Protocol
premise: Casper Ashgrove, a xenolinguist haunted by dreams that arrive in no human tongue, ferries mail and silence along the Long Route, a trade circuit of colonies that cut contact with Earth generations ago. When he intercepts a distress call in Vessari—a language exterminated, along with its speakers, in the Meridian Purge that official archives insist never happened—he realizes the signal is a recording loop, the last transmission of a hidden Vessari enclave, still broadcasting for help two centuries too late. Pursued by Concord agents determined to preserve the official history, Casper gathers a ragtag found family of route-dwellers who help him decode the loop, locate the enclave's surviving archive, and broadcast the truth of the massacre to every world on the Route before Earth's final transmission window closes forever. In the end, the Route speaks Vessari again—not as a dead language, but as a living vow of memory—and Casper, who never belonged anywhere, finds he belongs to the people who chose to remember.
about_author: Freya Thackeray is a former shipping-log archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of routes that no longer exist. She writes science fiction about the languages we abandon and the families we assemble from the wreckage.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A routine mail run between the colonies of Thessaly Reach and Cold Harbor establishes his lonely life, his dreamless sleep broken by alien syllables, and the Route's fading connections. He delivers a letter to a woman whose recipient died decades ago, and cannot bring himself to tell her. Emotional beat: quiet ache of a man who belongs to no one and nothing.

chapters.title: Static with a Shape
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Monitoring dead frequencies out of habit, he catches a repeating pattern in the noise between Cold Harbor and Meridian Station—structured, rhythmic, deliberate. His translation implants, tuned to extinct languages, respond before he does. Emotional beat: the first thrill of recognition, quickly shadowed by dread at what the language is.

chapters.title: Vessari
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with a flashback to his academy years studying the Purge-that-wasn't. He confirms the signal is Vessari, a language officially extinct for two hundred years, and decodes its opening phrase: 'We are still here.' Emotional beat: vertigo—the impossible made audible, and the suspicion that someone wants it unheard.

chapters.title: The Concord Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At Meridian Station, a polite Concord archivist named Ilse Vann inquires about 'anomalous transmissions' and offers Casper a lucrative contract to hand over his logs. He lies for the first time in his career. Emotional beat: fear crystallizing into defiance; invisibility is a choice he can no longer afford.

chapters.title: People Who Fix Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He turns to the Route's found family: Juno, a salvage engineer with a smuggled antenna array; the Okafor twins, who run the last independent relay; and old Bram, a retired teacher who remembers Vessari songs from his grandmother. Emotional beat: tentative warmth—the first time Casper asks anyone for help in years.

chapters.title: Bram's Grandmother's Song
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The old man listens to the loop and weeps, recognizing a lullaby his grandmother sang before the family erased its own heritage to survive. He gives Casper a hidden cache of Vessari phonograph cylinders. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance—memory passed hand to hand against all official history.

chapters.title: What the Loop Says
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Decoding deepens: the signal is a distress recording from a hidden Vessari enclave that survived the Purge for a generation before Concord found it. Its final line names the location of a physical archive. Emotional beat: the massacre becomes personal—names, children, a teacher's last lesson.

chapters.title: Erasure, Form 7-C
chapters.summary: Ilse Vann's POV. We see the machinery of denial: Concord's Archive Division rewriting records, Vann's own growing doubts, and her orders to seize Casper's ship 'with prejudice.' Emotional beat: a true believer beginning to crack under the weight of what she's erasing.

chapters.title: The Relay War
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Concord shuts down the Okafor twins' relay to cut Casper off. The twins, Juno, and a dozen route-dwellers rebuild the link overnight from salvaged parts while Concord patrols circle. Emotional beat: found family in action—many small hands doing one impossible thing.

chapters.title: Running the Dark
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He flies his aging ship through an uncharted debris field toward the coordinates in the loop's final line, with Vann's cutter on his tail and Bram's cylinders as his only cargo. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose—he is finally carrying something that matters.

chapters.title: Meridian's Bones
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He finds the enclave: a hollowed asteroid settlement, its walls covered in children's handwriting, its archive intact behind a door that opens to the lullaby. Emotional beat: awe and horror—the proof exists, and it is a home that was murdered.

chapters.title: The Archive of the Still Here
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Inside the archive: full records of the Purge, testimony recordings, and a message left by the enclave's last teacher, addressed 'to whoever finally answers.' Casper records his reply. Emotional beat: he answers a call two centuries old, and in doing so stops being a bystander to history.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Ilse Vann's POV. Vann boards Casper's ship at gunpoint, but Casper plays her the teacher's testimony—the voice of a woman who sounds exactly like Vann's own erased grandmother's generation. Emotional beat: confrontation as conversion; the archivist hears the archive she helped bury.

chapters.title: The Defector's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ilse Vann's POV. Vann must choose: report the archive and complete the erasure, or burn her career and help broadcast the truth. She transmits a false 'all clear' to Concord, buying Casper time. Emotional beat: the cost of conscience, paid willingly.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The team learns Earth's final scheduled transmission to the Route—its last contact in history—ends in nine days, after which the deep relay closes forever. If the truth doesn't ride that window, it may never reach the inner worlds. Emotional beat: a ticking clock that turns memory into urgency.

chapters.title: Assembly of the Route
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At Cold Harbor, route-dwellers gather—haulers, hermits, station-keepers—each contributing transmitter power, codes, and courage to boost the broadcast. Bram teaches the crowd the lullaby. Emotional beat: the Route, so long silent, finding one voice together.

chapters.title: Concord Descends
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Concord warships arrive at Cold Harbor demanding the archive and Casper's arrest. The crowd refuses to move; the twins jam the blockade; Vann publicly defects, presenting her own Division credentials as proof the cover-up exists. Emotional beat: standoff—fear versus solidarity, with the broadcast minutes from launch.

chapters.title: We Are Still Here
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. As Concord marines board, Juno fires the relay. The Purge records, the teacher's testimony, and the lullaby flood every world on the Route in Vessari and in translation, riding Earth's final transmission window inward. Emotional beat: climax—the dead speak, and this time everyone listens.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Voice
chapters.summary: Ilse Vann's POV. Across the Route, colonies answer the broadcast in Vessari, some fluently, some brokenly, all sincerely. Concord's command fractures; inquiries begin. Vann surrenders herself as evidence. Emotional beat: catharsis—erasure undone not by force but by memory, multiplied.

chapters.title: What Casper Dreams Now
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper's dreams, once wordless, now arrive in Vessari—and, for the first time, in the voices of friends. He catalogues the enclave archive properly, every name entered, every testimony heard. Emotional beat: healing—belonging arriving not as a place but as a practice.

chapters.title: The First New Word
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram opens a small school at Cold Harbor; the first lesson is the lullaby, the second is a new word the community coins for 'the ones who answered.' Juno, the twins, and Vann take their places in the room. Emotional beat: found family formalized—inheritance flowing forward at last.

chapters.title: A Signal for the Protocol
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, final chapter. Casper flies the Long Route again, mail and memory in his hold, the enclave's beacon now answered by thousands of voices. Earth's silence no longer means the end of the story. He sends one last message to the dead enclave: 'Received. Remembered. We are still here.' Emotional beat: resolution—grief transformed into continuity, and a man once invisible now unmistakably, permanently heard.
